title: Alfredo sauce with poultry and added vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Alfredo sauce with poultry and added vegetables is a creamy sauce made from Parmesan cheese, cream and butter, enriched with pieces of boiled chicken (or turkey) and a mix of vegetables such as broccoli, carrots and peas. The sauce offers a smooth buttery flavor complemented by the savory notes of poultry and the freshness of vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic Alfredo sauce was created in the early 1920s at the restaurant "Alfredo" in Rome.
Adding chicken boosts the protein content and makes the dish more satiating.
Vegetables not only enhance taste but also increase the vitamin and mineral profile of the meal.
While traditionally served with pasta, this sauce is also delicious over rice, couscous or in casseroles.
The combination of Parmesan cheese and chicken broth intensifies the umami flavor.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Parmesan cheese contributes calcium and phosphorus, supporting bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and vegetables supply B6, B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Broccoli, carrots and peas are rich in vitamin C, beta‑carotene and other antioxidants.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Butter and cream provide monounsaturated fats that, in moderation, can support cardiovascular health.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The cream and butter make the sauce calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream, butter and cheese may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk or cheese should avoid this product.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Parmesan and added salt can increase sodium intake; those with hypertension should limit added salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sauce hot over pasta, rice, couscous or as a casserole base. Add the sauce to the finished dish a few minutes before serving to heat evenly. Garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley or basil for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and gently reheat, stirring to prevent separation.
